learning.title: A route path is a string, so the type checker cannot see it
learning.symptom: A test module passes `deno check`, passes `pnpm lint`, passes `pnpm typecheck`, and 404s on its first request. Nothing in the static gate is red, so the failure looks like a fixture or a server problem on the first run.
learning.cause: Every route path in a test is a template string. The type checker types it as `string`, the linter has no rule for it, and the reviewer reading a diff sees a plausible path. `const SOURCES = "/v1/external-ticket-sources"` reads like the sibling of `/v1/external-tickets` and is not a registered route - the route table registers `/v1/ticket-sources`. A test can therefore be type-clean and wrong on its first line.
learning.rule: For a path, a route name or any other string the server resolves at runtime, the static gates are blind by construction - only execution closes it. That makes an unexecuted change an unpriced one: a declared "not yet run" is the only thing standing between a plausible path and a live one, and it must be declared out loud rather than implied by green checks. When relocating or copying test code, copy the constants from the module that own them instead of retyping them from memory.
learning.evidence: Bakery #69 / PR 540. Moving a case out of `tests/helpers/ticket-admission/operations-integration.ts` into `tests/integration/read-the-tickets-linked-to-one-task_test.ts` retyped the source path as `/v1/external-ticket-sources`. `ticket-actions.ts:92,101` registers `/v1/ticket-sources` and `ticket-routes.ts:25` guards it, so the preview call would have answered 404. `deno check`, `pnpm fmt` and `pnpm lint` were all clean at that commit; the defect was found by reading the route table, not by any gate, and fixed in `443ab7e96`. qa-qa named the class during review: the fix depended on the observation, and the observation needed the run.
